title: Zonal control-plane IP allocator and egress SG adaptor for private installer
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Private control-plane provisioning in multi-AZ customers exposed two operational challenges: (1) unpredictable ENI IP assignment across AZs that caused route-table overlap and late-stage kube control-plane failures during upgrades, and (2) inadequate security group attachment semantics for egress proxies where tenants need zone-anchored egress policies without changing core control-plane SGs. This PR introduces a zonal control-plane IP allocator and an egress-security-group adaptor to address both problems in an idempotent, Terraform-first way. Summary of changes: - New Terraform module: zonal_controlplane_ip_allocator (modules/network/zonal_ip_allocator) that reserves stable /32 IPs per control-plane instance per AZ using an idempotent tag-based allocation and a namespaced state key so customers can re-run provisioning without collisions. The module supports a migration path from the legacy ip-pool by optionally claiming existing ENIs. - Egress SG adaptor: a small controller and Helm chart values (charts/private-installer/templates/egress-sg-adaptor.yaml) that maps logical egress profiles to per-AZ security groups and attaches them to control-plane ENIs via instance-tag lookup. The adaptor is deployed as a sidecar-capable DaemonSet in on-prem flows and as a Deployment for VPC-based private control planes. - Installer changes: private-installer Terraform plan now wires the allocator module outputs into control-plane ENI resources and adds conditional outputs for cross-account peering routes. Added smoke checks and a migration toggle (feature_flag.migrate_zonal_ips) to convert existing clusters safely. - Helm/values: new values.private.controlPlane.zonalIP.enabled and values.egress.adaptor.enable for toggling in upgrades. Existing defaults remain off to preserve backward compatibility. - Tests & CI: terraform validate, fmt, unit tests, and a new integration harness (tests/integration/zonal_ip_simulator) that simulates AZ failure and verifies allocator idempotency. A constrained e2e run was executed against the staging VPC to validate SG attachments and DNS resolution across peering. Approach and rationale: - Deterministic allocation: We allocate per-AZ deterministic IPs by deriving an allocation index from the VPC CIDR and AZ hash to avoid centralized counters in state that cause contention in large fleets. The allocator stores a small set of tags on the allocated ENI and a TF-managed tag entry so subsequent runs can reconcile in-place. - Safeguarded rollouts: The default is off. The migration toggle performs a dry-run reservation, emits warnings for conflicts, and requires explicit manual approval in the Console or CLI to execute the migration. - Minimal blast radius: The egress SG adaptor attaches ephemeral per-AZ SGs instead of mutating core control-plane SGs. This lets tenants test egress policy changes per-AZ and roll back quickly. Rollout plan: - Stage 1: Feature merged behind flags; enable in a single non-prod region and run the migration tool in dry-run mode. - Stage 2: Canary: enable migrate_zonal_ips=true in one customer region with automated cutover window and on-call monitoring. - Stage 3: Gradual enablement: Open opt-in for customers via Console and then broad enablement after two weeks of canary stability. Testing performed: - Local integration: ran tests/integration/zonal_ip_simulator with 3 AZs simulated; allocator was idempotent across repeated apply/destroy cycles. - Staging VPC: Terraform apply used the allocator; DNS/peering smoke passed; adaptor attached per-AZ SGs and traffic shaping validated using iperf. - CI: terraform validate, terraform plan, helm lint, unit tests, and integration smoke passed. Known limitations and follow-ups: - Windows on-prem flows still use legacy ENI binding; follow-up ticket ENG-4240 will add Windows support. - Edge-case overlap in extremely small CIDRs (/28) will surface a validation error; added preflight check to block allocation in those cases. - Observability: added allocator metrics (alloc_attempts, reconcile_duration) to the installer metrics bundle but we need dashboarding; tracking INF-1001. Related work: references to prior PRs that handled control-plane subnet handoff and conditional DNS (see SUP-3312). This PR also introduces a small migration helper CLI (bin/migrate_zonal_ips) that is gated by RBAC. Security review notes: adaptor performs least-privilege AWS calls (DescribeNetworkInterfaces, ModifyNetworkInterfaceAttribute, CreateTags) and we added an IAM policy template with minimal actions and a short expiry token recommendation for on-prem automation.
